subject: Renewal pricing: conditional uplift + one-time credit structure
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@novaretail.com>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <rajiv@novaretail.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal pricing: conditional uplift + one-time credit structure

Hi Elena / Rajiv,

Thanks again for the time last week — appreciate the transparency on Q3 volume expectations. Based on the numbers you shared, I put together two practical paths to renew that keep your effective $/token close to current levels while giving you flexibility if usage spikes. High level:

- Option A: 12-month renewal with a 15% list discount + 120k one-time usage credit applied to any overage in Q1.
- Option B: 24-month renewal with a 10% list discount, a 6-month price hold for model list price, and a capacity uplift (reserve pool) that gives a 20% burst buffer at the same committed rate.

Both options assume the same baseline commit (120M tokens/month) with a rolling true-up each quarter. The one-time credit in Option A is intended to smooth your seat-up period if Q3 ramps faster than anticipated. Option B trades a slightly lower immediate discount for price stability and burst capacity.

I attached a short usage export and the term-sheet draft (renewal-term-sheet-v2.docx) for the finance team. Can we schedule a 30-min call Monday to walk this with Rajiv and your procurement lead? I’ll loop in Ben (SE) and Priya (AM) so we can answer technical, cost, and implementation questions in real time.

Next step: quick call + preferred option so I can draft a clean amendment.

Thanks,
Marcus

Thanks Marcus — quick notes after reviewing:

- We like the simplicity of Option B but the 10% discount still leaves us ~12% above our budget target for year 1.
- Procurement wants a firmer cap on price movement if we commit 24 months (they dislike open-ended list price exposure after month 6).
- Can you convert the Q1 one-time credit into an invoice credit that applies across the first two bill cycles? That helps with internal accounting.

Also, if we can get an additional 2% off the list on Option B (so 12% total) and a guaranteed price ceiling for the first 12 months, we can move forward to legal.

Elena — thanks for the clear ask. Looping Ben and Priya to validate technical/ops constraints and how we would operationalize the invoice credit. Notes below on what we can commit to and open items: 

- Concession: We can move Option B to a 12% list discount (was 10%) if NovaRetail confirms a 24-month term with the baseline commit you proposed.
- Price ceiling: We can guarantee a 12-month price ceiling equal to current model list for all covered SKUs. After month 12 standard list applies with 60 days notice for any list increases.
- Invoice credit: Instead of a Q1 usage credit, we can issue a one-time invoice credit split across the first two invoices (applied to month 1 and month 2 billing).
- Burst buffer: We’ll reserve a 20% burst pool on the committed capacity for months 1–3; usage beyond that will roll into standard true-up.

Open items for alignment: exact wording for price ceiling (Priya, can you confirm legal/regulatory language we should use?), and how we represent the invoice credit on the SOW/invoice (Ben, finance mapping).

If that looks OK I’ll capture as a marked-up term sheet and propose a canary amendment for signature via DocuSign. Proposed call: Sun 19 Jul 1:00pm ET. If that doesn’t work we can do Monday morning.

—Marcus

Thanks all — joining the call. Couple of operational clarifications up front: 

1) "Price ceiling" language: suggested phrasing we typically use — \"Redwood will not increase model list prices for any covered SKU during the first 12 months following effective date; any list price change thereafter will be communicated 60 days in advance and will not retroactively apply to usage incurred prior to the change.\" Please review and tell me if legal needs a stricter cap.

2) Invoice credit flow — finance: we will issue a single credit memo at contract effective date and apply 50% to invoice 1 and 50% to invoice 2. This preserves their accounting requirement for an invoice-applied credit.

3) Burst pool: implementing the 20% reserved burst for first 3 months requires a short ops playbook (auto-route to dedicated burst pool). Ben, I can share the config quickly — will you confirm performance expectations if they hit the pool?

If those three items are fine, Marcus, please mark up the term-sheet and I’ll prepare the operational appendix so legal has a concrete SOW.
